buckets.label: What you need to know today

items.headline: ₹33,000 cr government securities underwriting auction adds supply pressure, likely nudging 10‑yr G‑sec yields up
items.what_happened: The government announced an underwriting auction of ₹33 bn of dated bonds scheduled for Oct 23.
items.why_it_matters: Extra supply in the dated‑bond segment can lift benchmark 10‑yr yields, raise corporate borrowing costs and affect duration exposure in fixed‑income portfolios.

items.headline: Repo auction cut‑off rate of 5.54% signals tighter short‑term liquidity and pushes INR‑linked short‑term yields higher
items.what_happened: The overnight variable‑rate repo auction on Oct 22 allotted the full ₹50 bn at a cut‑off of 5.54% and a weighted average of 5.55%.
items.why_it_matters: Higher repo rates raise money‑market rates, lift short‑end G‑sec yields and increase funding costs for banks, which can pressure the INR and equity valuations.

items.headline: Weighted average overnight money‑market rate at 5.64% indicates sustained high short‑term funding cost
items.what_happened: Money‑market operations on Oct 21 show a weighted‑average overnight rate of 5.64% (range 4.85‑6.00%).
items.why_it_matters: Persistently high money‑market rates keep short‑end yields elevated, supporting INR pressure against a strong USD and influencing cost‑of‑carry for equity positions.

items.headline: SEBI’s Third Amendment to AIF Regulations tightens compliance reporting, raising audit workload for alternative‑fund managers
items.what_happened: The Securities and Exchange Board of India issued the Alternative Investment Funds (Third Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
items.why_it_matters: The amendment adds new disclosure and reporting obligations for AIFs, meaning CA clients will need to update compliance processes and may incur higher audit fees.
items.action: Notify AIF‑related clients to review the new regulations and adjust their reporting calendars this week.
items.update_note: Carried over from yesterday with new reporting.

items.headline: RBI clarifies minimum Cash Reserve Ratio stays at 90%, confirming no easing of bank liquidity buffers
items.what_happened: The RBI issued a notice stating that scheduled banks must maintain a CRR of not less than 90%.
items.why_it_matters: A unchanged CRR limits banks’ ability to expand credit, sustaining current funding‑cost dynamics and supporting the outlook for short‑term rates.
